1984.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four — Wikipedia
1984.summary: Nineteen Eighty-Four (also published as 1984) is a 1949 dystopian novel by English writer George Orwell. Set in the superstate Oceania, it follows Winston Smith, a low-ranking Outer Party member who secretly rebels against the omnipresent surveillance and propaganda of the Party led by Big Brother. Central themes include totalitarianism, mass surveillance, historical revisionism, and the manipulation of language through Newspeak. The novel introduced the English lexicon to terms such as 'Big Brother', 'doublethink', 'thoughtcrime', and '2 + 2 = 5'.

1984.title: 1984 — Reader Reviews (4.5 / 5 from 28,412 ratings)
1984.summary: Aggregated reader reviews of 1984. Average rating 4.5/5 across 28,412 ratings. Reviewers most frequently praise the prose's clarity, the prescience of the surveillance state, and the emotional weight of the Winston-Julia relationship. Common criticisms include a slow middle section (Goldstein's book excerpts) and the bleakness of the ending. Frequently recommended alongside Brave New World, We, and Fahrenheit 451.

1984.title: 1984 — Full Text (Public Domain Mirror)
1984.summary: Complete text of Nineteen Eighty-Four in three parts. Part One opens: 'It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen.' Part Two covers Winston's affair with Julia and his recruitment by O'Brien. Part Three contains the Ministry of Love interrogation, Room 101, and the final scene at the Chestnut Tree Café. Appendix: 'The Principles of Newspeak.' Approx. 88,900 words.
